saints.name: St. Aelred of Rievaulx
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A Cistercian abbot of Yorkshire whose gentle writings on friendship and charity earned him a lasting name…
biography: Born at Hexham in 1110, the son of a married priest of that ancient church, Aelred spent his youth at the court of King David I of Scotland, rising to be steward of the royal household. In 1134, at twenty-four, he left it all for the new Cistercian abbey of Rievaulx in Yorkshire.

Made novice master, then abbot of the daughter-house of Revesby in 1143, he was chosen abbot of Rievaulx in 1147 and ruled it twenty years, while the community grew to some one hundred and forty choir monks and five hundred lay brothers. His gentleness made him a father rather than a master to his monks.

His Mirror of Charity was written at Bernard of Clairvaux's asking; his Spiritual Friendship, finding Christ at the heart of human friendship, is his best-loved work. He also wrote histories for King Henry II and a rule for his sister, a recluse.

Worn for years by the stone and arthritis, he died at Rievaulx on 12 January 1167 and was buried in the chapter house beside Saint William, the first abbot. Never formally canonized, his cult was confirmed by the Cistercians in 1476; David Knowles called him the Bernard of the North.
saints.knownFor: His writings on spiritual friendship and charity.
